messages:
scanner-bot: Scheduled vuln scan failed: repo=infra/terraform-docker, job=nightly-scan, 03:12 UTC.
scanner-bot: Error when fetching submodule 'modules/private-images': HTTP 401 unauthorized
scanner-bot: log:
```
GET https://git.internal.redwood/services/private-images.git/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack => 401
caused_by: token authentication failed for user 'scanner-ci'
```
maria: Ugh, that's my fault — I rotated the Snyk/Git token for scanner-ci last Thursday during secret hygiene sweep and forgot to update the CI secret. :facepalm.
ash: can we confirm this was Snyk token vs GHAS app? the 401 implies credentials not accepted, not rate limit.
maria: it's Snyk token used by the scanner to fetch submodules (we proxy via Snyk in the workflow). I rotated the KMS envelope for the token and forgot to rewrap the new secret into the vault path used by the scanner.
devon: do we currently pull the raw token from KMS or do we use a service key stored in Vault? we should have scanner fetch via Vault->KMS unwrap flow. if it fetches plaintext from env, that's the fragility.
kevin: scanner service uses Vault transit for wrapping but the CI job reads from GitHub Actions secrets for hosted runners and from vault for self-hosted. looks like this repo runs self-hosted runner in infra project that reads /secret/scanner/ci-token which still pointed to old ciphertext.
maria: i'll update the vault value in 10m. quick question: will this token rotation require a new GHAS permission grant? or just update the secret?
akash (sec-ops-bot): FYI, we had a recent incident where suppression rules hid a high severity vuln because the scanner allowed auto-suppression for 'devDependencies' without justification. we should ensure this change doesn't re-enable any risky suppressions. :warning:
ash: related — while we patch the token, can we also run a targeted full scan (no suppressions) for infra modules? want to catch anything the suppression rules are currently hiding.
sec-ops-bot: Agreed. Propose we temporarily run Trivy in 'strict' mode and GHAS SCA without suppression for a single run. I'll open a quicksec ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-423 
oncall-eric: noted. Also watch for KMS decrypt errors — last week we saw intermittent KMS permission errors during key rotation window. If vault rewrap coincides with KMS key rotation it may throw 403s.
devon: action items: 1) maria updates vault ciphertext for /secret/scanner/ci-token (maria) 2) kevin will trigger an ad-hoc strict scan run and post results (kevin) 3) sec-ops will run suppression audit and add mandatory justification field to any suppression rule that auto-ignores >=HIGH (sec-ops) 4) oncall-eric to monitor KMS logs for decrypt failures during the change window.
maria: will do step 1 now. I'll post the vault audit entry.
kevin: triggering strict scan now, ETA ~15m. please don't touch runner configs while it's running.
maria: vault updated and audit entry: "rotate scanner-ci token" -> https://vault.internal.redwood/audit/entries/9876
scanner-bot: Re-run result: failed again for a different reason: 403 Forbidden fetching submodule, error: access denied for user 'scanner-ci' despite valid token.
kevin: we hit a permission boundary on the git side — the token scope doesn't include access to the private submodule repo. looks like when token was rotated it was created with repo:read but not repo:submodule.
maria: fixing token scopes now, will generate a new token with the correct scopes and re-wrap to vault.
sec-ops-bot: Reminder: when you re-create tokens, tag secrets in Vault with rotation metadata and ticket link. We'll require a short justification field on the suppression policy change PR.
maria: done — new token created, wrapped, and pushed. PR #2384 updates scanner creds + documents rotation steps. linking: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2384
kevin: strict scan completed — no HIGH vulns suppressed this run. github-actions results: summary attached, sending to #security-reports.
sec-ops-bot: We'll follow up with a small RFC to require suppression justification and a scheduled quarterly suppression audit. I'll draft SEC RFC and assign owners.
ash: thanks everyone. follow-up: let's add an automated alert when a scanner-run hits any 4xx/5xx fetching vcs artifacts, and include the root cause (auth vs rate-limit) in the alert. can we add that to the scanner's telemetry?
devon: yes — i'll add http-status tagging to the metrics and a small rule in pagerduty to route auth failures to sec-ops and config failures to infra.
maria: closing the loop: token rotation fixed, strict scan clean, suppression audit started. will update SEC-423 and the PR with final notes. :white_check_mark:
